artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact symplectic $2n$-manifold equipped with a completely integrable system $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon M\to\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. the components $f_i$ Poisson-commute with respect to $\omega$ and are functionally independent on a dense open set. Assume that the singularities of $F$ are non-degenerate in the sense of Williamson, so that every singular point admits local symplectic coordinates in which $F$ is, up to an analytic equivalence, a sum of components of regular ($\partial/\partial\theta_i$), elliptic ($x_i^2+y_i^2$), hyperbolic ($x_iy_i$), and focus-focus ($x_iy_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i,\ x_iy_i+x_{i+1}y_{i+1}$) type.

Suppose $(M,\omega)$ carries a prequantum line bundle $(L,\nabla)$ with curvature $\omega$, and let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the real polarization tangent to the fibers of $F$. The geometric quantization of $(M,\omega,L,\mathcal{P})$ is defined as the sheaf cohomology
$$\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P}) = \bigoplus_{k\ge 0} H^k(M,\mathcal{J}),$$
where $\mathcal{J}$ is the sheaf of sections of $L$ that are flat along $\mathcal{P}$. For polarizations whose only singularities are of regular and non-degenerate elliptic type, a sheaf-theoretic scheme (a Čech-type computation localized at Bohr–Sommerfeld leaves) yields a finite-dimensional quantization space concentrated in a single degree.

Problem. Modify this sheaf-theoretic quantization scheme so as to produce a finite-dimensional representation space $\mathcal{Q}(M,\mathcal{P})$ in the presence of focus-focus and hyperbolic singularities, in such a way that the resulting invariants still encode the symplectic semi-local invariants of those singularities (e.g.\ the Vũ Ngọc Taylor series for focus-focus, and the affine-length / Dufour–Molino–Toulet invariants for hyperbolic singularities) and, more generally, the symplectic invariants of the underlying integrable system.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Miranda, Presas and Solha (arXiv:1705.06572) and the cotangent-model approach of Miranda and collaborators (e.g. arXiv:2102.02699) provided modifications yielding finite-dimensional quantization spaces in the presence of focus-focus and certain hyperbolic singularities for semitoric and almost-toric systems, cancelling the infinite-dimensional contributions seen in earlier schemes. A complete scheme capturing all symplectic invariants of these singularities in full generality does not yet appear in the literature, so the problem is best described as partially solved.
